description:
Verifies that a mobile or CTV app bundle ID actually exists in the
relevant app store — used to detect bundle spoofing in bid requests.

Platform support (v1):
- `ios`: verified live via Apple's iTunes Lookup API.
- `android`: verified live via the Google Play store listing page.
- `ctv_*` / `web`: no public store API — returns verified=null.

Inputs:
- `bundle_id` (body, required): e.g. `com.nytimes.NYTimes`.
- `platform` (body, required): ios | android | ctv_roku | ctv_fire |
  ctv_samsung | ctv_lg | ctv_vizio | web.
- `claimed_developer` (body, optional): checked against the store listing.

Returns:
- `verified`: true | false | null. null means one of two things: the
  platform has no store API (confidence `low`, warning
  `no_store_api_available`), or the store lookup failed (confidence
  `degraded`, warning `store_api_unavailable`, with `reason`).
- `reason`: why the store lookup failed — http_<status> | timeout |
  network_<error name> | bad_response. Present only on the degraded path.
  When the relay was also tried and failed it is
  `<worker reason>+relay_<relay reason>`, e.g. `http_403+relay_timeout`.
- `source` (iOS only): `worker` | `relay`. When the Worker's own iTunes
  lookup ends in http_403, http_429 or network_* and the relay is
  configured, the lookup is retried once through TunnelMind's relay;
  `relay` means the relay was consulted (success or failure).
- `store_listing`: name, developer, developer_match, store_url.
name: sigil_verify_app_bundle
